_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: Backspace on a pill ahead of a partial term keeps query and list in sync. The browser's requests carry the header X-ExeDev-Email: me@example.com, so the current user is me@example.com. The test harness has already stubbed the server's conversation list and cut off its live update stream, so there is nothing to set up, intercept or check about that (do not look at the API): the drawer (".drawer") shows the conversations the test names, as rows [data-conversation-id="<id>"] whose title (".conversation-title") is their slug, which is their id (drafts have none), and whose preview is "Preview". The list is "mine" (written in by me@example.com and other@example.com, tagged alpha), "other" (other@example.com) and "alpine" (third@example.com, tagged alpine). "The tag panel" is data-testid "tag-filter-panel"; its entries are [data-tag="<tag>"]. "The count" is ".drawer-filter-result-count". "The user pill" is the ".conversation-query-token-value" inside the token user:me@example.com. window.__drawerErrors lists the page's uncaught errors and console.error messages. The search query editor is the contenteditable element with data-testid "conversation-query-editor" ("the editor"); its data-query-value attribute is the serialized query. "The query is X" means data-query-value is exactly X, spaces included. To "set the query to X": eval the editor's focus(), press_key "a" with modifiers "Control" (the editor's own select-all), insert_text X (as pasting would), then wait until the query is X. To "clear the query": eval the editor's focus(), press_key "a" with modifiers "Control", press Backspace, then wait until the query is "". Query tokens are [data-conversation-query-token="<kind>"] elements inside the editor (kind tag or user); "the token T" is the one whose text contains T. Perform the numbered steps in order, each fully. A button "X" is {"role": "button", "name": "X", "exact": true}, with a "selector" to scope it when it is a row's, a menu's or a group's; but "there is no button X" counts {"role": "button", "name": "X"} without exact, so that a name containing X counts too. Texts that "are exactly [...]" are checked with assert_texts. "There is no S", "no S" or "none" means no element matches at all: assert_count 0, never a visibility check. Whether an element "has the class X" is an eval of its classList.contains('X') (polled with expect), never a visibility check: a collapsed drawer may have no size. Every selector you need is given here, so do not explore the source code or read other tests (the old Playwright spec is being replaced and does not apply): write all the steps in one run_steps call right away, and look something up only if a step fails. 1. Navigate to /new. 2. Click the button "Search conversations...". 3. The query should be "user:me@example.com ". 4. The count's text should be exactly "2" (the new conversation's draft row passes the participant scope too). 5. A trailing partial tag: click the user pill, then type "tag:al" key by key. 6. The query should be "user:me@example.com tag:al"; the tag panel's [data-tag="alpha"] is visible and it has no [data-tag="alpine"]; the count's text is exactly "2". 7. Click the user pill again, which puts the caret right after its separator. 8. Press Backspace. 9. Removing the pill shifts the partial left and the edit follows it: the query should be " tag:al" (with the leading space); there are no user tokens; the tag panel's [data-tag="alpha"] and [data-tag="alpine"] are both visible (the participant scope is gone). 10. Press Escape. 11. There should be no tag panel; the query is still " tag:al"; the count's text should be exactly "4"; [data-conversation-id="other"] and [data-conversation-id="alpine"] are visible. 12. Eval "JSON.stringify(window.__drawerErrors)" must be exactly [].
